stories.headline: Malik Nabers Is Back on His Feet in Jersey and the Saloon Hasn't Adjusted Its Price
stories.read: Ten months after that busted wing put him down in Week 4, Nabers rejoined team drills this week, planting and cutting hard off the rebuilt knee and looking the best he has all summer. He won't promise anybody he's ready for Dallas on September 13, and that's exactly the kind of hedging that keeps a fella cheap. Here's Doc's read, pardner: this is a man who commanded a monstrous cut of the throws before he got laid up, and nobody else on that roster is close. Every day he practices without a setback, that discount gets a little thinner. Go stake the claim while the herd is still spooked.

stories.headline: Stefon Diggs Rides into Washington, and Somebody's Cut of the Throws Just Got Smaller
stories.read: Washington made it official this week: one year, twelve million, and Diggs lines up opposite Terry McLaurin with Jayden Daniels slinging it. The man went 85 catches for a thousand-and-change in New England last year and finished as the seventeenth-best receiver in the whole territory, so this ain't a charity hire. What it means for your outfit is simple arithmetic: Diggs is a fine mid-to-late-round horse on a real offense, but every other pass-catcher in that camp just got squeezed. Deebo Samuel's replacements and the young fellas behind McLaurin are dry wells now. Adjust your board before the fellas you're ridin' against do.

stories.headline: Luther Burden Is the Most-Hunted Man at Bears Camp and That's Cheap Gold
stories.read: Every dispatch out of Chicago says the same thing: Burden is the most-targeted man on that field, day after day, and Ben Johnson's staff can't stop talking about how far he's come. Rome Odunze still holds the top spot at the ranch on paper, but paper don't catch footballs. Doc's angle: the second-year leap is a tricky ride, sure, but a fella soaking up that many throws in August is the exact shape of a strike waiting to happen, and the saloon is still pricing him behind Colston Loveland. That's a vein nobody's dug yet. Grab him three rounds past where he's worth and let your leaguemates read about it in October.
